lines: A browser multiplayer pirate treasure race. The game is specified in [`docs/spec.md`](docs/spec.md) (the text of `docs/spec.docx`); [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) maps this repository onto it.

-Browsers create or join a private match by a six-character code and sail placeholder ships around the slice sea: a compact map with four small islands with docks, reefs and shoal walls that funnel every route between islands through one central crossing, and eight outer-sea spawn slots. Up (or W) sails ahead, down (S) brakes and then reverses, left and right (A, D) turn, and E docks a ship beside a dock, at any speed. The authoritative server decides every position and sends each browser only the ships within its sight radius; the minimap's fog clears where the player has sailed.

+A match can be played and won end to end (§2, §5). Browsers create or join a private match by a six-character code and gather in its lobby, which lists the players; the host starts once two or more are in (late arrivals are refused). A 20-second countdown follows while the arena loads, then player control starts with 45 seconds of departure protection and the 35:00 timer counting down. The first player to hold every rubbing type is told the exact route to the final island (a compass, an arrow and a mark on the minimap), and everyone learns its sector in a banner; minute 20 and minute 28 bring more reveals. Stop inside the treasure circle holding every type and hold E for ten seconds to win: moving, letting go, losing a type, disconnecting or being grappled resets the claim, and any rival in range can grapple you. The match ends with the winner, or with no winner at the deadline, and every browser shows the results: each player's rubbings, thefts, losses, duels, gold, caches and islands.

+Ships sail placeholder hulls around the slice sea: a compact map with four small islands with docks, reefs and shoal walls that funnel every route between islands through one central crossing, and eight outer-sea spawn slots. Up (or W) sails ahead, down (S) brakes and then reverses, left and right (A, D) turn, and E docks a ship beside a dock, at any speed. The authoritative server decides every position and sends each browser only the ships within its sight radius; the minimap's fog clears where the player has sailed.

Fights happen at sea (§6): J grapples the nearest ship ahead within six tiles. The attacker sees its aim, the target a warning with the side it comes from, and it lands after a one-second windup unless the target sails out of range or out of the aim (a miss costs six seconds). A grapple that lands stops both ships; after a three-second countdown the two fight the online duel inside the match, in the same page's arena, while everyone else in sight sees crossed swords and the elapsed time where they fight. The winner sails on with eight seconds of protection; the loser respawns at a dock 15 seconds after the fight, with 20 seconds of protection; a draw returns both to separate nearby points.

The race is for rubbings (§4; the slice plays Sun and Moon, two sealed sources on each island). Moor at an island's dock and keep holding E: after six seconds you collect its rubbing of a type you lack (the HUD shows what the island holds, only while you are moored there, and the hold's progress). Win a duel at sea and, within five seconds, press 1 or 2 (or click) to steal one of the loser's types you lack, with 20 % of their gold (the rarest type is taken if you do not choose; a draw moves nothing). The purse beside the game shows your gold, your rubbings and what the last duel took or gave, and whether the winner chose it or the default took it. A player who drops keeps their seat, ship and rubbings for 60 seconds (a fighter away from a duel for ten seconds forfeits it); one who never returns, or quits, leaves a recovery cache at a dock, a chest others see when in sight. Moor there and hold E to claim one rubbing of a type you lack.

The map is generated from an ASCII sketch of one quarter, `assets/source/maps/sliceSeaSketch.ts`: edit it, then run `npm run map:build -- --from-sketch` (details in `assets/source/maps/README.md`). The `.tmj` stays within the Tiled subset documented in `packages/content/src/tiledMap.ts`, so [Tiled](https://www.mapeditor.org/) opens it.

-`PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_PLACEMENT=1` is a test-only setting, off by default: the dev and test entry point (`npm run dev`, and the server the browser tests start) then serves `POST /__test/place`, which puts a player's ship on a chosen tile. `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_SOURCES` (for example `sun,sun|moon,moon|sun,sun|moon,moon`, each island's source types) is another, off by default: every match then deals its rubbings in that layout instead of the private shuffle. The production entry (`npm start`) reads neither.

+`PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_PLACEMENT=1` is a test-only setting, off by default: the dev and test entry point (`npm run dev`, and the server the browser tests start) then serves `POST /__test/place`, which puts a player's ship on a chosen tile. The others, also off by default: `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_SOURCES` (for example `sun,sun|moon,moon|sun,sun|moon,moon`, each island's source types) deals every match's rubbings in that layout instead of the private shuffle; `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_TIMINGS` (for example `ready=60,protection=20,match=12000`, in world ticks, 20 a second; also `sectors` and `carriers` for the two timed reveals) shortens the countdown, the departure protection, the match and its reveals; `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_FINAL_SECRET` (a 32-bit number) pins the secret that picks the final island. The production entry (`npm start`) reads none of them.

The integration tests run in two groups (`npm run test:integration`): most files in parallel worker processes, with test-only shorter timings, then the netcode harness files (`duelHarness`, `seaDuelHarness`, `devLatency`) one after another on a quiet machine.

content.text:
A match can now be played and won end to end: lobby, 20 s ready countdown, the 35:00 timer, reveals, a 10 s claim, and a results screen. All five policy checks pass locally with all nine browser scenarios. Per the workflow rules nothing is committed; the changes are in the worktree.

**Checks I ran:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck` | 0 errors |
| `npm run test:unit` | 53 files, 1,230 tests pass |
| `npm run test:integration` | 16 files, 89 tests pass in 157 s (budget 300 s; it was 122 s before) |
| `npm run build` | smoke test passes, and now also checks production ignores the new test-only settings and opens in the lobby with the 20 s countdown and 35:00 timer |
| Full Playwright suite | 10 passed |
| JSON-reporter run of every spec, then the pinned `check-report` | all 9 scenarios ok, including `full-match` |

**What changed:**
- **Room (`apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts`):**
  - **Lobby:** the host starts at 2 or more players, using the match module's `PRIVATE_MIN_PLAYERS`. From the countdown on, joins are refused with "That match has already started".
  - **Control start:** every ship gets the 45 s protection. The claim deadline and the timer are built from one config (`matchFlow.ts`), and tests assert they are equal.
  - **Tick order:** encounters → the ledger's collect/claim holds → claim → match flow → intel reveals.
  - **Endings:** claim, deadline, abandoned, and aborted (any world tick that throws is treated as a server fault).
- **Hidden information:** everyone gets the sector; only the full-set holder gets the exact point. An integration test checks the other player's raw frames never contain it.
- **Seeds:** one `node:crypto` master secret per match, with an HMAC-SHA-256 seed per system (`matchSeeds.ts`). The ledger deal now uses it. Tests show the seeds differ per system and never depend on the match code.
- **Protocol v7:** `start-match`, `start-refused`, `reveal`.
- **Test-only settings**, all off by default and never read by `main.ts`:
  - shortened timings;
  - a pinned final-socket secret;
  - an injectable master secret;
  - `testHooks`: a fault injector, plus a clock pause that lets tests land a grapple on a claim's completion tick and complete a claim exactly on the deadline tick.
- **Web (`flowHud.ts`):** lobby panel, clock bar with the timer and sector, reveal banners, compass plus treasure circle and minimap mark, and a claim panel with the risk line. Also a warning when a rival in sight is claiming, and a results screen with "Back to lobby".
- **New tests:** `lobby`, `reveals`, `claim` and `endings` integration files; web and protocol unit tests; the `full-match` browser scenario. The existing scenarios now start through the lobby; single-player tests use a second "companion" player.
- **Carry-forwards:** all four done (key auto-repeat ignored, the Phaser.AUTO comment, the invariant assertion in `seaDuelHarness`, the dock-reuse unit test).
- **Docs:** `docs/architecture.md` has a new "lobby to results" section, and `README.md`, `docs/encounters.md` and `docs/objectives.md` are updated.

**Decisions I made that you should know about:**
- **Players are named by seat ("Player 2") in the lobby and results, not by session id.** Putting ids in the public state would have broken the existing test that a ship's id first reaches a client when the ship comes into sight.
- **Cancelled duels count as neither won, lost nor drawn** in the results.
- **Stale constant, not fixed:** `privateMatch.minPlayers` (1) in `packages/content/src/rules.ts` is outside my paths. Nothing reads it now; it needs a later content cleanup.

**Not covered by any test:**
- The "you lost a type" claim reset can't happen while claiming, because a duel's reservation resets the claim first. The pure claim module covers it; the room test covers "can't restart the claim after losing a type".
- A second eligible player waiting while another claims.
- The rival-claim warning in a real browser (unit-tested only).
- An abort caused by a real exception (only the injected fault is tested).
- Disconnecting during the lobby or countdown.

The completion file is written to `match-online-001/game.completion.json`.
